# Temple Scroll Column 44 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 44 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 44:1 — "detestable thing" vs. "abominable thing" vs. "anything that is detestable" — to'evah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "any detestable thing" | Project standard rendering |
| LOGOS | "any abominable thing" | Elevated formal term |
| PNEUMA | "anything that is detestable" | Expanded phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "any detestable thing" per EMET. Consistent with project rendering of to'evah/sheqetz terms.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 44:5 — "hare" vs. "hare" vs. "rabbit" — arnevet identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the hare" | Traditional biblical rendering |
| LOGOS | "the hare" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the rabbit" | Modern colloquial equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the hare" per EMET and LOGOS. "Hare" is the established biblical term for arnevet.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 44:12 — "detestable" vs. "abomination" vs. "detestable" — sheqetz rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "detestable to you" | Project standard |
| LOGOS | "an abomination to you" | Formal term |
| PNEUMA | "detestable to you" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "detestable" per EMET and PNEUMA majority.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 44:13 — "sojourner" vs. "resident alien" vs. "foreigner living in your town" — ger rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sojourner who is within your gates" | Project convention for ger |
| LOGOS | "the resident alien within your gates" | Formal legal status term |
| PNEUMA | "the foreigner living in your town" | Modern accessible rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sojourner" per EMET and project convention established in the Pentateuch translations.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 44:14 — "holy people" vs. "people holy" vs. "people set apart" — am qadosh rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a holy people to the LORD your God" | Literal word order |
| LOGOS | "a people holy to the LORD your God" | Slightly varied word order |
| PNEUMA | "a people set apart for the LORD your God" | Dynamic — interprets qadosh |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a holy people to the LORD your God" per EMET. Direct and faithful to the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 44:15 — "kid" vs. "young goat" vs. "young goat" — gedi rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a kid" | Traditional biblical English |
| LOGOS | "a young goat" | Clarifying expansion |
| PNEUMA | "a young goat" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a kid" per EMET. "Kid" is the established English term for gedi in this famous prohibition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 44:16 — "judgments" vs. "ordinances" vs. "rules" — mishpatim rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "judgments" | Literal mishpatim |
| LOGOS | "ordinances" | Formal legal term |
| PNEUMA | "rules" | Simplified modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "judgments" per EMET. Consistent with project rendering of mishpatim.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
